## Part 4 · 31:21

[31:21] That promise was enough to sustain the small community of believers at the beginning, and it will be enough to uphold the church in the darkest days of the end. It is the driving force of history. But here a crucial question arises. If he promised to return, what should we do while we wait? Simply sit and stare at the sky? Jesus' answer is a resounding no. Right after he conquered death and before he ascended to the Father, he left one final instruction, a command for all.

[31:59] Before ascending to heaven, Jesus said, "Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature." It wasn't a suggestion, it was a command, a mission for everyone. And it's significant that this charge came right after his resurrection and just before his return to the Father. Because Jesus wanted one thing to be unmistakably clear. Waiting for his return was never meant to be passive, but active, marked by proclamation.

[32:30] The same one who promised to come on the clouds also said, "And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come." Here Jesus tied the spread of the word directly to the climax of history. The end will not arrive by chance or by human decree, but when the message of the gospel has reached the very ends of the earth. That's why sharing the word is not merely an act of kindness, it is fulfilling a prophetic condition that sets the stage for his coming. Joy and hope for some, and chaos, confusion, and despair for others.

[32:57] For in a split second, the entire world will be torn apart. The trumpet will sound, the dead in Christ will rise, the living will be caught up, and in that very moment, the earth will be emptied of millions. Heaven will be filled, but the earth will sink into indescribable chaos. The planes that crisscross the skies will be left without pilots. In a single heartbeat, passenger-packed aircraft will plunge into cities, seas, and mountains. The roar of shattering metal will mingle with the screams of survivors.

[33:34] Control towers will lose contact with dozens of flights at the same time, unable to fathom why so many planes vanished from radar all at once. Schools will fall silent. Thousands of desks will be filled one second, and the next, they'll sit empty, backpacks and notebooks strewn across the floor. Teachers will look up to find half their students gone.

[34:44] The echo of empty chairs will fill the rooms, a silent scream no one can explain. Desperate parents will race to schools and daycares in search of their children, only to find buildings in chaos, teachers weeping, crowds in hysteria. In churches, the scene will be even more overwhelming. Some pews will be empty, others will remain packed with bewildered faces. Faithful pastors will vanish mid-sermon, leaving their congregations in a tomb-like hush. But in other churches, where the gospel had been watered down into prosperity and entertainment, many will be left behind.

[35:19] Their cries will tear through the sanctuaries. Men and women pleading through tears, pounding the pews, realizing too late that the warnings they had scorned were true. Some pastors who had preached a comfortable, crossless Christ will remain standing facing the accusing eyes of their flock. News outlets will panic. Cameras will capture crowds vanishing from the streets, planes nose-diving, hospitals overflowing. Governments will try to calm the masses, but their voices will be thin against a horror no one can hide.

[35:58] Social media will live-stream the collective hysteria, showing entire cities collapsing under the sudden absence of millions. Families will be split in two. Husbands who mocked the faith will wake to find the bed beside them empty. Unbelieving children will weep when they see their parents are gone. Homes will fall silent, meals still on the table, lights still on, children's toys still on the floor, but no children. Every house will become a memorial to what was lost in an instant.

[36:28] It will mark the dawn of a new world, a world without the church, without the salt that preserves and the light that guides. And that void will open the way to confusion, to fear, and to a desperate search for a global leader with answers. It will be the fertile ground for the Antichrist to rise. For the rapture will left the world in ruins, streets overflowing with chaos, families shattered, governments staggering, economies in freefall. And in the midst of that confusion, a desperate need will emerge.

[37:03] Someone with answers, someone to explain the unexplainable, someone to offer peace in the middle of the collapse. That will be the perfect stage for the Antichrist to appear. Scripture calls him by many names, the man of sin, the son of perdition. John saw him as the beast rising out of the sea, the little horn in Daniel's vision, or the lawless one. Different names, but the same figure. He won't come with violence at first. He won't raise his voice like a tyrant from the start.

[37:36] He will arrive as a savior, the man who can unite enemy nations, calm the crowds, rebuild the economy, and promise global security. Paul says his coming will be in accordance with Satan's activity, with great power, signs, and lying wonders. In other words, he will deceive not only with words, but with visible miracles. He will call down fire from heaven. He will perform wonders that will astonish the whole world, and multitudes will receive him as the man who brings peace after the chaos of the rapture. He will be charismatic, persuasive, seductive.

[38:08] Many will call him the leader the world needed. But behind that facade will lurk the greatest lie in history. Daniel saw his rise centuries earlier. In his vision of the beasts, he describes a little horn that overthrows others, that grows and speaks arrogantly against the Most High. That horn represents this world leader, unlike those before him, with an authority that will devour every nation. John confirms the vision in Revelation, "And authority was given to him over every tribe, people, language, and nation." Never before will the world have been so unified under a single government.

[38:44] His rise will be swift, fueled by global desperation. He will make a seven-year peace accord with Israel, the famed covenant with many. At first, he will look like a hero. He will allow the temple in Jerusalem to be rebuilt, broker alliances between enemy nations, and proclaim stability. But it will all be a carefully planned deception. And halfway through those seven years, his true nature will be laid bare. He will enter the temple of God and sit as though he were God himself, demanding worship. This is what Jesus called the abomination of desolation.

[39:23] From that moment, the great tribulation will begin, 42 months in which the Antichrist will ruthlessly pursue anyone who refuses to bow before him. Revelation describes how he will enforce an absolute economic order. No one may buy or sell without the mark on the right hand or the forehead, the infamous number 666. It will not be merely a symbol, but a tool of total control. Whoever rejects the mark will be cut off from the system. No food, no work, no way to survive daily life. But whoever accepts it will have sealed their eternal fate.

[40:00] For receiving the mark will mean surrendering to the power of Satan and definitively rejecting Christ. The Bible does not show him acting alone. There will be a false prophet, a religious leader who performs signs to convince the masses to worship the beast. Together, they will form an unprecedented political religious system. The Antichrist will raise up an image of himself that comes to life and will demand that all worship it. Whoever refuses will be executed.

[40:36] It will be the return of an imperial cult on a global scale, like in the days of Rome, only now armed with technology, counterfeit miracles, and absolute control. His arrogance will be total. He will speak great blasphemies against God. He will exalt himself above every so-called God and every object of worship. He will promise peace, but bring destruction. John says the dragon, Satan, will give him his power, his throne, and great authority. He will be, in essence, the embodiment of satanic deception, a false Messiah seeking to take the place of Christ.

[41:08] Those left behind will begin to understand the words they heard so many times yet never believed. They will remember the sermons that warned of a time of anguish unlike anything the world has ever known. They will remember that Jesus himself spoke of a tribulation so intense that if those days were not shortened, no one would survive. Then they will realize that what is beginning is not a period of peace, but the prelude to the wrath of God. And what will happen to those who repent? Will there be a second chance? Those who awaken too late will feel the crushing weight of their mistake.

## Part 5 · 41:43

[41:43] Yet right there, on the brink of despair, a clear choice will stand before them. Resist. Resist the system the Antichrist will impose. Resist the mark that will become the passport to buy and sell. Resist even if it means losing everything, even your life. It will be a time of spiritual preparation like no other. Empty churches will fill again, but no longer with lukewarm crowds, rather with broken men and women weeping on their knees, knowing there is no time left for religious games.

[42:20] Pastors who were left behind will rise with courage, now preaching the truth they once withheld, knowing their days are numbered. Entire communities will forge secret covenants of loyalty to Christ, committing to refuse the mark even when the pressure becomes unbearable. They will call one another the sealed. They will share the last piece of bread. They will hide together. They will die together. Homes will become modern catacombs. The Bible, once ignored and gathering dust, will become the most precious treasure.

[42:51] Every page will be read through tears, every promise memorized as provision for days of famine and persecution. On dark nights, small groups will gather in basements, caves, and secluded homes, breaking bread and praying, knowing they could be discovered at any moment. Yet this resistance will carry a terrible cost. There will be public executions of those who refuse the mark. Prisons will overflow with new believers who once despised the faith. Families will be torn in two, some surrendering to the system, others remaining faithful to Christ, knowing it will cost them their lives.

[43:25] But for many, there will be hope. For the scriptures assure that a great multitude will be saved in the midst of tribulation. And what seemed a final, definitive end will become a second chance for millions. The Apostle John saw it in a vision. After describing the chaos, he wrote, "After this I looked and behold, a vast multitude that no one could number, from every nation, tribe, people, and language, standing before the throne and in the presence of the lamb." Astonished, John asks who they are. The answer is the key to it all.

[44:01] The angel replied, "These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation. They have washed their robes in the blood of the lamb. They are the ones, the ones who were left behind, who woke up late, but who, in humanity's darkest hour, chose to stand firm. What seemed like a final condemnation became their second and last chance. Their shed blood will join the cry of the martyrs, and their faithfulness in the fire will stand as an eternal testimony. They weren't the ones taken in the rapture, but they were the ones who, in the end, chose Christ, no matter the cost.

[44:38] The Bible opens windows into the past that reveal how God follows the same pattern. He rescues his own first, and then he brings judgment. Noah's story echoes the rapture. For years he built an ark in obedience while the world mocked him. No one believed judgment would come as waters that would cover the earth. But the day came when God himself shut the ark's door. It wasn't Noah who locked himself in. God sealed the refuge. Outside the crowds were swept into destruction. Inside, the righteous family was secure. So it will be at the rapture.

[45:14] A door will close in an instant and the world will be left outside. The same happened with Lot. Genesis 19 tells how the angels took him and his family by the hand and led them out of Sodom before fire fell from heaven. Lot hesitated, like many who struggle to leave behind what's familiar. Yet even so, in his mercy, God pulled him away from the doomed city. Jesus used this example when speaking of the end. So it will be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed. The lesson is clear. Before judgment, God always delivers his own. The parallel is obvious.

[45:50] In the days of Noah, people ate, drank, and married, ignoring the warnings. In the days of Lot, people were buying, selling, and building, never imagining their world would be reduced to ashes. Jesus said, "It will be the same when the Son of Man comes." The world will carry on with its routine, ignoring the signs until suddenly the door is shut and the righteous are taken out. God never pours out his wrath on the righteous together with the wicked. He always separates, always rescues, always keeps.

[46:27] He did it with Noah, he did it with Lot, and he will do it with the church before the tribulation consumes the earth. It will be a repeat of an ancient pattern, but on a global and final scale. From the opening chapters of scripture, God had already shown that he has power to snatch his servants away, to move them from the earth into his presence without passing through death. There were other raptures in the Bible. Enoch was the first. Enoch walked in a corrupt world in a generation nearing the flood. Then, before judgment arrived, he was caught up without seeing death.

[46:59] We read, "Enoch walked with God and he was no more because God took him." Enoch did not die, was not buried, did not remain on the earth. One day, he simply was gone. The community looked for him, but they did not find him. Enoch is the earliest echo of the rapture. God took a man who walked with him and caught him up from the earth before judgment. Centuries later, another prophet would confirm this pattern. Elijah, the prophet of fire, ended his ministry in a way that defied all human logic. As he walked with Elisha, a chariot of fire appeared between them and carried him off in a whirlwind.

[47:35] Elisha watched him ascend, and all he could do was cry out in awe. Elijah never knew a grave. There was no tomb, no mourning, no burial. He was caught up to heaven in glory. Elijah was taken in the midst of his mission, leaving an indelible testimony that death is not the only possible end for the righteous. His being caught up was visible, spectacular, accompanied by fire and wind, a glorious preview of what will happen on a global scale when the church is taken in the twinkling of an eye. But even in the New Testament, God granted a preview of this mystery.

[48:13] Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles, recounted a unique experience. In 2 Corinthians 12, Paul confesses that he was caught up to the third heaven. He doesn't know whether it was in the body or out of the body, but he knows he was taken into paradise and heard inexpressible words, things impossible to convey in human language. It was a brief transport, a drawing back of the veil to confirm that heaven is real, that the rapture is possible, that God can carry a person into his presence in an instant. Paul wasn't describing a simple dream.

[48:49] It was a real translation, a spiritual rapture in which he experienced the glory of heaven ahead of time. These three witnesses, Enoch, Elijah, and Paul, are prophetic signs pointing to the same end. God has the power to take his own without their passing through death. Three testimonies from three different eras, yet one pattern, the catching away of his people before judgment is poured out. This isn't a new theory. It's a divine principle. The rapture of the church will only repeat on a universal scale what God has already done on an individual scale.

[49:24] That's why we must not forget what is written. These aren't words for debate, but signs to remember, not theories for speculation, but certainties to keep us standing. The rapture will be the moment that divides history forever. In the blink of an eye, the earth will be thrown into chaos and heaven will fill with glory. What is an unseen hope today will be an undeniable reality tomorrow. Christ will do what he promised. He will come back for his own. Remember the signs. Jesus will appear in the heavens. The trumpet of God will resound. The dead in Christ will rise.

[49:59] The living will be transformed. We will meet the Lord in the clouds. We will be with him in glory. And until that day comes, let's encourage one another with these words. For we are not called to walk alone, but to remind each other of the hope that sustains us. And remember, the mission isn't to keep this message, but to spread it. The world needs to hear these signs. Time is running short and there are millions who still don't know, who still aren't ready. Share this video with your loved ones, your friends, with everyone you can.

[50:35] It's how the message multiplies, how the gospel reaches more people. But the most important question is, are you ready? If the rapture happened today, would you be caught up? Would you be prepared? I want to invite you to leave your answer in the comments. Be honest. Share your faith, your reflections, even your doubts. Let's make this space a place where we can encourage one another, remembering the promise is real and that Christ is coming for his own. Let's encourage each other. The rapture is closer than ever and Christ is coming. But the rapture is just the trailer.

[51:08] What really matters is knowing what comes after, which signs are real and which ones are deceptions, and most importantly, what God does with the people who are still here. To understand what's actually happening at the end of days and how to protect yourself, you need to watch the video that's on screen right now. In it, you'll see the signs that help us understand where we are on God's prophetic timeline and how much time is left before the end. If you stop at the rapture, you stay in spectator mode. If you understand revelation, you're prepared.
